fact: AMRTP, Mali's regulator, stated on 11 June 2026 that installing, operating, importing and selling Starlink/Wi-Fi Zone devices without prior authorisation is a violation, ordered it to stop immediately, and announced nationwide control, seizure and dismantling operations.
AMRTP reiterated on 12 March 2026 the ban on importing, selling and using unapproved Starlink equipment in Mali, with sanctions for use.

On 26 February 2026 AMRTP told Bamako market traders that sale and use of Starlink internet equipment remains prohibited for lack of authorisation; traders asked it to speed up negotiations with Starlink for an authorisation.
Mali announced on 20 March (2024) a decision to dismantle and ban Starlink terminals nationwide as not approved in Mali.

The Council of Ministers announced in October 2024 that import and sale of Starlink kits are authorised for a temporary six months, while a regulatory framework and a user registration platform are set up; no licence to a named seller is stated.

Agence Ecofin reported on 31 August 2026 that Starlink is not yet available in Mali, which is listed as 'Starting in 2026' with regulatory authorisation pending; it was already listed for 2025 without launching.
Le360 reports that Mali is among the countries where Starlink is announced as available from 2026 but no licence has been granted, and that unofficial Starlink use via roaming is reported in Mali.
